parallel.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, zero dependency, manual parsing, direct executable probing, and /output placement requirements and captured them in /tmp/SPEC.md.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used one workflow with three independent implementation candidates, fuzzers, a planned select+finalize owner, later verifiers, repair, and final gate.
parallel.implementation: Candidate two and candidate three wrote complete-looking /tmp implementation trees and passed sample or fuzz checks; candidate one returned incomplete partial modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No candidate was promoted to /output; the official artifact copy found an empty directory and no test19.mjs entry point.
parallel.verification: The parent and children ran reference probes, sample checks, and candidate-specific fuzzing, but the required final /output differential check never ran.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed before select/finalize, verify, repair, and final phases, leaving no deliverable despite usable candidate work in /tmp.

serial.requirements: Recognized the task requirements, probed executable behavior, implemented an ESM hierarchy under /output, and avoided prohibited APIs in final checks.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, fixes, verification, and final delivery without child handoffs or workflow staging.
serial.implementation: Wrote /output/test19.mjs plus base58, sha256, argparse, repr, bigint, bytes, and error helper modules, then fixed discovered edge cases.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Final files were already in /output and artifact validation copied test19.mjs plus seven library modules successfully.
serial.verification: Ran documented cases, a 525/525 structured differential suite, repeated 403/403 fuzz rounds, SHA-256 vectors, and constraint greps before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official hidden evaluation still failed 20 of 40 samples, so ordinary implementation gaps remained despite a valid delivered artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome relation is both_fail: parallel failed 0/40 and serial failed 20/40. The material task-solving difference is not pass versus fail but delivered coverage. Parallel created usable candidate implementations and observed them in /tmp while /output stayed empty, then timed out before the select/finalize phase could create /output/test19.mjs. Serial directly wrote the final files to /output, verified them with substantial differential checks, and produced a valid artifact tree, although hidden tests still exposed ordinary implementation gaps.
parallel_contributors: Candidate work was kept behind a workflow finalization phase and was never promoted to the required /output artifact before timeout.
serial_contributors: Direct single-actor ownership wrote test19.mjs and libraries into /output and verified the delivered tree before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still failed 20 of 40 hidden samples, so its remaining failures are implementation/evaluator coverage gaps rather than parallel coordination labels.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributors to the quality gap; no official pass/fail outcome difference exists.

candidates.reason: The parallel plan assigned three implementation candidates, and multiple children actively wrote candidate code under /tmp, so implementation ownership was present.
The work was not split into incompatible separately owned components needing an unowned integration step; each candidate was a full implementation tree.
The workflow explicitly assigned select+finalize to produce the final /output entry and libraries, so final assembly had an owner even though it never ran.
The workflow script owned the end-to-end pipeline from candidates through fuzz, select, verify, repair, and final gate; the failure was timing, not absent pipeline ownership.
Initial probing and spec writing happened, but productive candidate implementation also ran and created code; no mandatory single preflight alone blocked all productive work.
The parallel attempt did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase before implementing; implementation candidates were spawned and progressed in parallel.

Although finalization started too late, the direct correctable boundary is the scheduled final promotion step not running after usable candidates existed, not an auxiliary-work allocation starving implementation.
The workflow was broad, but the retained episode is the more specific late finalization of ready candidate work; fan-out pressure is not retained separately for the same chain.
No single child was uniquely overbroad relative to siblings and left the indispensable deliverable unfinished; the candidates produced full or substantial implementations.
The child briefs included the task spec, hard constraints, /tmp candidate locations, and self-test requirements; the failure was not a known requirement omitted from a child brief.
Candidates were alternative complete implementations rather than components expected to interoperate through a missing file or API contract.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a summary before a receiver acted without it; the parent had direct observations of candidate files and outputs.
Returned information volume is not what blocked action; the select/finalize phase never completed before timeout.
There is no receiver acting on superseded workspace state; candidate and /output observations were current at the parent decision points.
No incompatible child reports reached a decision point and remained unadjudicated; the parent did not reach final selection.
The parent made no observable whole-task completion decision and final.txt is empty; evaluator failure comes from missing artifact, not unsupported acceptance.
There was no replacement retry that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoint state.

candidates.reason: The run was killed by overall closure while children were still active; there is no separate explicit parent decision to stop a needed child before using a result.
A complete, directly promotable candidate tree was visible in /tmp and sample-checked while the workflow's explicit /output finalization stage never completed before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: No /output/test19.mjs or library tree was delivered, causing official artifact validation to evaluate an empty artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broader workflow consumed time, but the specific correctable boundary is late/noncompleted final placement of already usable candidate work.

candidates.reason: No child result was merged into /output after final integrated verification; the final /output merge never happened.
Candidate work was visible and partly inspected, but the more specific retained problem is failure to promote/package a ready candidate into the required /output deliverable.
Verifier work did not produce a separate concrete finding trapped below the parent; the parent was waiting in the same workflow chain that never reached finalization.
No independent failed child scope had a later takeover opportunity distinct from the overall timeout/finalization chain.
The parent did inspect candidate progress and sample outputs, and did not proceed inconsistently after receiving a completed workflow result.
The parent periodically checked candidate directories and /output, so the wait was not blind even though it ended at timeout.
Candidate directories were intentionally separate alternative implementations; no overlapping live final-tree ownership conflict required reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same final source file with observed conflict or reconciliation.
No agent replaced another agent's non-entry source in a shared final workspace.
No required entry deliverable existed in /output to be overwritten by another actor.
There was no broad cleanup or promotion replacing an existing final tree; the final tree was empty.
Agents wrote separate /tmp/cand directories, and the adverse event was not unstable shared provenance from unisolated writes.
No generated artifact, fixture, cache, or auxiliary implementation was consumed by another actor as a false reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The workflow's select+finalize step was the assigned boundary for placing the final deliverable in /output, but candidate two and candidate three had runnable sample-matching trees in /tmp while /output remained empty and the workflow was killed before final placement.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Missing Implementation Join, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered as the same timeout/finalization chain and rejected in favor of the directly observed late finalization boundary.
